newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek equities recoup early losses, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Greek equities recoup early losses, close higher.

text.p: Greek equities recouped early losses to close higher after a late session buying spree that helped the benchmark share index settle with gains of 0.20 percent in moderate turnover.

"October and November are historically difficult months for the stock market because of the preparation of next year's budget. I see more quiet torture ahead up to mid-November. stocks could slide a little more," said investment advisor Iakovos Diamantopoulos at Hermes Brokerage.
"But smart money should be buying equities during this period, it is in my view a buying opportunity because recovery will come and returns will be relatively fast and attractive," he said.

Brokers have attributed the market's recent slide to law 2396/96 which outlines the general framework governing the activities of firms offering investment services in Greece, harmonising Greek law with European Union legislation.
It has sparked selling as players were forced to close out long margin positions, they said.
The Athens general share index closed up 0.20 percent, or 1.88 points higher at 920.34 from Tuesday's 918.46 close after opening at 918.88 points.
Turnover fell to 5.78 billion drachmas from 8.34 billion on Tuesday on volume of 4.0 million shares.

Losers led gainers 125 to 75 with 34 issues unchanged on 234 traded. Banks gained 0.71 percent, industrials slipped 0.34 percent with construction rising 0.95 percent after plunging 4.43 percent on Monday, still trading near all time lows.
Small-caps settled unchanged, down 0.04 percent after tumbling 4.02 percent on Monday.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas closed higher at 544-562. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended up 25 drachmas at 4,075.

The Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares ended higher at 163.90-172.50 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It closed in-the- money at 1007.7

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $9.74-$10.74. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 3,918-4,163 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
